pages.title: Telomerase Complex
pages.text: An enzyme that rebuilds telomeres - the protective caps at the ends of chromosomes that shorten every time a cell divides. Cells that have it do not age. The complex is small, pale and oddly cold, as if keeping time for itself.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Telomerase is real; most adult cells have switched it off. The Evolution Engine ran a million generations of stem cells and tardigrades with Turing morphogens and Xenoplasm, while an arrow of time shard kept the clock running fast.
